subject: Aurora bench: prioritization & runbook
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-05-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Aurora call recapper + bench asks

Quick recap from the 11:00 call with Aurora (Elena/Kyle) — they asked for a short, prioritized A/B bench and a clear decision matrix comparing Redwood hosted vs their current hyperscaler endpoints. Key customer asks: p95/p99 for 128 & 512 tokens, sustained tokens/sec at 100 concurrent users, and a runbook for fallback behavior when p99 spikes.

Action items I captured:
- Internal: define a 2-day A/B bench (Redwood hosted vs Aurora's hyperscaler endpoint) with identical prompt set and load profile. Prioritize p95/p99 and tokens/sec. (Owner: Neha)
- Workload: Elena said they'll provide a representative sample payloads and expected concurrency; ask for both short-chat (avg 64 tokens) and long-gen (avg 420 tokens) traces. (Owner: Aurora)
- Config: test with seq_len 128 / 512, batch sizes 1/4/16 where applicable; measure tail latency and 1-minute sustained throughput. (Owner: Aditya)
- Decision matrix: capture cost per 1k tokens (estimate), p95, p99, and graceful-degradation behavior (cache hits, model fallbacks). We want to recommend a configuration that meets their p99 SLA target (<= 400ms for short-chat) or show tradeoffs. (Owner: Marcus)

Neha/aditya — please add specific test commands and infra needs by EOD so I can send the runbook to Elena and lock a test window for next Tue/Wed. I attached the suggested runbook template and csv layout for raw output.

Attachments: runbook-ab-config.yml (template), aurora-p95p99-raw.csv (output schema)

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-25T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora call recapper + bench asks

Marcus — thanks, clear notes. Quick clarifications and proposed test plan below.

On 2029-05-25 at 15:10 Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick recap from the 11:00 call with Aurora (Elena/Kyle) — they asked for a short, prioritized A/B bench and a clear decision matrix comparing Redwood hosted vs their current hyperscaler endpoints.

Proposed bench (high level):
- Day 1: Functional parity + correctness run (verify outputs are semantically comparable on our tuned model). Low concurrency (1/5 users) — capture tokenization parity and output diffs.
- Day 2: Performance sweep — run sequences at seq_len=128 and seq_len=512 with concurrency ramps: 50, 100, 200 users. For each ramp measure: p50/p95/p99, avg tokens/sec, CPU/GPU util, and 1-min sustained throughput.
- A/B config: Redwood default quant + dynamic batching vs Aurora endpoint using their standard instance type (we'll use their provided endpoint details).

Test instrumentations we need from Aurora:
- Representative sample_workload.json (they mentioned sending this)
- Baseline latency CSV from their side (if available) to avoid measurement skew

Infra notes (Aditya): can target our staging pool with isolated nodes; I'll bring up an empty namespace for Aurora so we can tag metrics. I think 8 GPUs on Day 2 for Redwood run should be sufficient to hit throughput targets without autoscale noise.

I'll draft the detailed command list and the bench script by EOD and attach run commands to the shared Drive link.

-Neha
Senior Infra SRE
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@aurora.ai>, Kyle Fisher <kyle@aurora.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-25T17:00:00-07:00
Subject: Aurora bench: prioritization & runbook

Elena/Kyle — thanks for the productive call today. Quick public summary and our ask to get the bench scheduled: 

What we'll run (short):
- A/B test: Redwood hosted inference (our recommended quant + batching) vs Aurora's current endpoint.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 tail latencies at seq_len 128 & 512; sustained tokens/sec under 50/100/200 concurrent virtual users; and failure/retry/fallback behavior.
- Test cadence: 2 days preferred (Day 1 correctness, Day 2 perf sweep).

What we need from Aurora to start:
1) representative sample_workload.json (both short-chat and long-gen traces) — please attach to the Drive link below or reply with the file
2) your baseline latency CSV (optional but helpful)
3) a 3-hour window next Tue or Wed for the Day 2 perf sweep (we will coordinate exact times)

We included a suggested runbook and the CSV schema for our result capture. Proposed decision criteria: if Redwood meets Aurora's p99 target for short-chat (<= 400ms) with comparable cost within 25% of their hyperscaler spend, recommend Redwood hosted; otherwise identify the tradeoff and a remediation plan (quantization/longer batching/hybrid routing).

Attachments: aurora-sample-workload.json (placeholder), runbook-ab-config.yml (template)

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/aurora-bench
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/deal/3481

Looking forward — once we get the sample workload I'll share the final command list and infra footprint.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — appreciated the clear plan. Attaching our representative sample_workload.json and a small baseline CSV export (aurora-p95p99-raw.csv) so you have our real numbers. We can do Wednesday 2029-05-29 09:00-12:00 PT for the perf sweep.

Notes from our infra team: our production endpoint uses instance-family z3.large with internal batching set to 8; we will keep the endpoint warm for the window. We expect average short-chat to hit p99 ~380ms today; would like to see how Redwood behaves at 100 concurrent users.

I uploaded the files to the Drive folder and added read access for neha@redwood.ai and aditya@redwood.ai.
